Source. For the exact staged witness, this reads the sole GeoStar payload word `0x20202020` from admitted message `0x22` and materializes `ul1 == 538976288` as the parsed `SVs in view` count.
The parsed count is copied into persistent session state without validation, so `session->gpsdata.satellites_visible` becomes the huge positive value `538976288`.
A present guard caps only the local loop bound `ul1` to `GEOSTAR_CHANNELS == 24`; it does not repair the already-stored `session->gpsdata.satellites_visible`, which remains `538976288`.

The parser populates at most the first 24 `skyview` entries and sets `SATELLITE_SET`, establishing the satellite-report path that later reaches `fill_dop`. The stored `satellites_visible` from step 2 is not changed here.
Control reaches `fill_dop()` because GeoStar parsing returned `SATELLITE_SET` and the corrupted `satellites_visible` field is a positive integer.

Root cause. The loop bound is the huge propagated `satellites_visible` value, not the actual `skyview` extent. `gpsdata->skyview` has only `MAXCHANNELS == 184` elements (`include/gps.h:2944`), so after the in-bounds iterations `k` still advances and the first out-of-bounds iteration is `k == 184`.

Sink. When step 6 reaches `k == 184`, this reads `skyview[184].used`, one element past the last valid array entry `skyview[183]`. AddressSanitizer reports this exact read as the global-buffer-overflow in `fill_dop`.

The DOP loop uses the attacker-influenced `satellites_visible` field directly as its upper bound and never clamps it to `ROWS(gpsdata->skyview)` before indexing `gpsdata->skyview[k]`.
AddressSanitizer crash site. Once `k` reaches the first index past `skyview[183]`, this boolean read dereferences one byte in the global redzone after the `session` object.
